question: In vasomotor rhinitis, ipratropium bromide nasal spray is the preferred treatment when watery rhinorrhoea is the dominant symptom, because it blocks the parasympathetic (cholinergic) drive to nasal secretory glands.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. This statement is true. Ipratropium's mechanism (anticholinergic blockade of secretory glands) directly targets the pathophysiology of the hypersecretory subtype of vasomotor rhinitis. Matching drug class to dominant symptom (hypersecretion vs congestion) is a key management principle.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Ipratropium bromide is an anticholinergic agent that blocks parasympathetic stimulation of nasal glands, effectively reducing watery hypersecretion. For patients whose dominant complaint is rhinorrhoea rather than congestion, it is the drug of choice in vasomotor rhinitis.
